transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there! Do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but after that, you can go back to light exercise such as gardening. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for letting me know. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Alright, that's good to know. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, is not normal and may need to be assessed further. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. This should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurrier, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay. If we put in a standard lens, it’s common to have difficulty reading as most lenses are for distance vision. This means you will need reading glasses or varifocals for reading, and that’s entirely normal if it’s the only part of your vision that is blurry. Unfortunately, I don’t have access to your medical records, so I don’t know what lens we put in. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you again!

verdict.label: pass
